overview: A Pacific system brings snow to the northern Rockies, the Cascades and the Northeast on Thanksgiving weekend, with Friday and Saturday the main snow days. Several western ranges also see weaker systems and a more active pattern returns early next week.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: A Pacific system moves into western Wyoming Thursday night and Friday, bringing light to moderate snow west of the Continental Divide. A second wave Friday night into Saturday brings wider snow and strong westerly wind, with the first light accumulating snow possible east of the Divide. Grand Targhee leads with 63" total. The NWS is calling for more, 21 to 32 inches Saturday night through Monday, though the NWS forecast here is not a confirmed storm total.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A moderate atmospheric river brings rain and mountain snow Thursday and Friday, with the wet pattern lasting about 50 hours. Snow levels drop toward 4,500 feet in the eastern Cascades Friday night through Saturday. Mt. Bachelor leads at 45" total, and Crystal Mountain sees rain mixing with snow Thursday before turning to snow Friday.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Whistler and Cypress see a mix of rain and showers through Friday, with snow mostly confined to the higher terrain. A front brings more showers to the Coast Mountains Sunday and Monday, and the cooler air late Monday adds some flurries. Whistler leads at 31" total.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: A strong low tracks north Thanksgiving Day and brings freezing rain to northern New York and Vermont Thursday evening into Friday, with slippery travel and a Winter Weather Advisory through Friday morning. Cold air is shallow, so the ice mainly stays above 1,500 feet. Jay Peak leads at 27" total, and Whiteface sees a Winter Weather Advisory Thursday through Friday as well. A frontal system brings more rain and snow Sunday night into Monday.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Thanksgiving stays mild and dry before a northwest flow sets up Friday through Saturday night. The Park Range looks favored for orographic snow, with confidence highest there and lower to the south. Snow may reach as far as Vail Pass, especially Saturday. Steamboat leads at 30" total, and Vail sees snow showers Saturday.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Rain Thursday turns to showers, with snow levels near 1,500 metres. Snow shows up again Sunday with a chance of flurries or rain showers, and a bit more is possible Monday. Whitewater leads at 23" total.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: Dry, seasonable weather holds through Thanksgiving. A weak Pacific trough brings light valley rain and mountain snow mostly north of I-80 Friday night through early Saturday, and another weak system crosses northern Utah Monday. Powder Mountain and Brighton see light snow in that window.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Dry and mild weather with dense valley and delta fog Thanksgiving through Saturday. Rain and high-elevation snow return Sunday and Monday, with snow levels near 7,000 feet. Sugar Bowl sees rain and snow Sunday and Monday, and Palisades gets rain and snow Sunday. The Sierra expects a more active pattern next week.

regions.title: Okanagan
regions.text: Showers end Thursday morning, leaving a mix of sun and cloud Friday and Saturday. Flurries and rain showers return Sunday, with cooler air and a chance of flurries Monday. Big White leads at 15" total.

regions.title: Canadian Rockies
regions.text: Showers Thursday give way to a mix of sun and cloud Friday through Monday, with a chance of flurries Sunday and cold air by Monday night. Sunshine Village leads at 7" total.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 25, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Dec 6–12. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
